target: UTM-bundled QEMU framework, HVF, two vCPUs, 1 GiB RAM, virtio-ramfb, VirtIO keyboard/tablet
command: QEMU=build/utm-qemu-probe/qemu-probe QEMU_VIRT='-L /Applications/UTM.app/Contents/Resources/qemu -machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -smp 2 -m 1024 -device virtio-ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device' ZEAL_COMPAT_LOG_PATH=build/check-keepaway-current-smp2-input-stress.log python3 -u scripts/check-compat.py --pci --quick --probe-3d-apps --probe-keepaway-full-game
result: Pass: KeepAway remained responsive through repeated gameplay input and recovered cleanly
checks: The game rendered its court and HUD, accepted Space and mouse input, and refreshed the HUD before the long run.
During the 186-second gameplay interval, the probe repeated pointer movement, left-click shooting, and brief Space presses 18 times.
Framebuffer scanout continued changing through the full run.
Escape returned to the graphical terminal with keyboard focus restored.
No Animate child task remained after exit and zstatus reported failed=0.
scope_note: This automated test uses UTM's bundled QEMU framework and the exact current ISO; it is not a visible UTM app-window test. It does not erase the user's visible UTM freeze report, but it shows that repeated pointer and gameplay input do not reproduce the freeze in this two-vCPU guest configuration.
